items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: I mean you follow some very good musicians who Mario Bauza had originally hired to be in the — oh man my brain is leaking

ctx.x: I’m trying to think of an example, we were talking about breaking down structures. I’m trying to think of an example of some progressive jazz where they broke down the harmonies and melodically but the dance oriented groove remained. Because it seems like as people broke down these parts of what we think of as music that they all were breaking down at the same time and what we got from that was sometimes free jazz. I’m not sure if I’m verbalizing my question but can you think of any musicians who sort of kept a…

Well yeah, they — well yes certainly. Like go back to bebop, Dizzy Gillespie was very, very interested in solving the relationship between the dance times of Latin music and the dance times of jazz. And the one is not in the same place, which was difficult at first for the musicians trying to cross that line. If you listen to the early recordings of the Gillespie orchestra with Chano Pozo you will see that they’re not always in the same place certainly at the very beginning. And later on as it got to “Tin Tin…
I should be able to help you out so I’m having one also.
